approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from a greedy population of scored molecules. It chooses parents across score quantiles, applies connected-fragment crossover and ordinary atom, bond and ring mutations, and rejects duplicate or unstable molecular identities. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. A final admission gate prevents a candidate from introducing more of any outside-envelope sulfur signature than the maximum present in its original scored generating parents. Each suggestion builds a full fresh surplus pool. A fixed Gaussian process learns from every earlier accepted task-local score using folded, chirality-aware Morgan occurrence counts and dot-product count Tanimoto covariance. It normalizes scores by the archive mean and population standard deviation, then chooses offspring with correlated sampled functions and sequential availability masks. Only real accepted scores update its archive and greedy survivors.
approach.novelty: Replace the allocation mean with the fixed exponential-GP mean while keeping the original count-Tanimoto residual distribution. This creates one hybrid Gaussian acquisition law: exponential conditional predictions guide the centre of each sampled function, while the Parent retains its original exploration covariance, random draws and sulfur admission rule. The earlier full exponential substitution improved some selected-stream prediction measures but lost endpoint score; it changed both paths together on an ungated Parent. This experiment changes only the mean path on the sulfur-gated Parent. There are no completed direct siblings in this brief. The complementary same-round partial-path experiment retains the original mean and changes the residual covariance; neither experiment establishes an interaction, transfers the old prediction improvement, or replaces the complete endpoint test.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting uncertainty in code Parent n-1744a1494180 is whether its original GP mean ranks the fresh alternatives usefully enough while preserving supported correlated exploration. Its three actual summary.json/run.log pairs complete the frozen panel with macro mean 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878 and seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287 and 0.583088384937917. The sulfur gate adds only +0.0007834645552323346 against its own Parent n-62daf219c70a, with one losing seed, and misses the separate +0.002 improvement goal. These endpoints do not prove a mean defect. The direct discrepancy is n-07dd356cb779: the full fixed exponential law improves same-selected-stream MSE 0.007744 to 0.007064, unequal-label pair accuracy 66.48% to 67.19% and Spearman 0.4279 to 0.4417 versus its passive original predictor, yet loses -0.032277693549492024 against ungated n-62daf219c70a; every deco-hop ranking cell worsens. Its relative parent beats increase from 629 to 697 while best-source and offspring absolute scores fall. n-299096e31fe7 loses -0.07686116167690966 when residual influence is removed, n-54adc6a641e8 loses -0.018447481386582327 when residual correlation is removed, and n-01b48dd09404 loses -0.12438789088524467 under generation-order allocation at unchanged pool/model effort. These conditional original-composition controls motivate retaining the original residual law, without proving its support transfers unchanged through the sulfur gate or that exponential means help. Reading all fifteen actual Parent optimizer logs gives 648 strict best-parent beats and 255 sequential incumbent advances among 4350 accepted offspring, with exact emitted-to-accepted joins and 435 full pools. These are Parent measurements, not inferred benefits of the new mean path.
hypothesis: Replace only the allocation mean with the fixed exponential-GP mean while retaining original count-Tanimoto residual covariance.

finding_summary.headline: Better selected-stream predictions accompany a 0.05827 endpoint loss; the mean route stops
finding_summary.insights: Improving prediction on the candidates the algorithm actually chose was insufficient for reliable endpoint progress. The hybrid ranks that selected stream slightly better than the original predictor computed on the same state, but its additional local wins occur against weaker generating parents and do not restore the lost absolute incumbent progress. The current test therefore rules out this fixed mean route as a useful endpoint improvement under the sulfur-gated profile and meets its one-test stopping condition. It does not show that exponential means always fail, or identify a mean/covariance interaction: the earlier full-law experiment used an ungated Parent. The molecular assessment finds recognizable aromatic and polar frameworks but continued reactive attachments, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry; fewer occurrences of one liability coexist with increases in others and chemically doubtful high-score exceptions. New graph cores and labels therefore do not establish credible independent chemical series or a chemical mediator. Pool-wide calibration, rewards of passive alternatives, transfer and unresolved retained-component composition remain open.
finding_summary.results: The declared law executed on all 435 full pools and delivered all 4,350 selected offspring with prospective predictions and correct accepted identities. Compared with the original predictor on those same accepted labels, unequal-label pair accuracy rose from 68.39% to 68.90%, mean defined batch Spearman rose from 0.4713 to 0.4825, and MSE fell from 0.006325 to 0.005811. The directions vary by task and seed; all cells and null batches are retained in the measurements. Strict parent beats increased from 648 to 720 and sequential incumbent events from 255 to 283, while mean offspring score fell from 0.37205 to 0.36349, mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.45530 to 0.41972, and total sequential incumbent gain fell from 5.81942 to 4.94538. Final Top-1 macro mean fell from 0.59645 to 0.53818: paired delta -0.05827, below the required +0.002. All three seed macros lost; only 3 of 15 task/seed endpoints improved. No evaluation, identity, numerical, fallback or timeout failure explains the loss.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, bulky azaheterocycles and aryl amines retain reactive attachments, difficult rings and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-14a52e3f8725 produced ring-rich aromatic amides/hydrazides, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl heterocycles, aromatic aliphatic amines, cyclic dicarbonyl frameworks and fluorinated heterocycles. All 15 Child and 15 published n-1744a1494180 Parent trajectories were present and read in full: each panel contains 900 accepted records per objective, including 870 optimizer observations and 30 initial observations over issued Search seeds 0/1/2. The trajectories describe accepted oracle-observed molecules, not the entire unlabelled surplus pools or rejected generator proposals. All digest exemplar tuples, score extrema and deterministic string counters were checked exactly. Child ring-closure text incidence is 0.9931-1.0 and aromatic-text incidence 0.9897-1.0; these are molecule incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Charge and stereocentre text incidences are 0.0 throughout. RDKit parses every accepted molecule; parse validity establishes neither geometric feasibility nor synthesis. Median optimizer heavy-atom counts range from 25 to 45 and perceived ring medians from 3 to 7. Recognizable medicinal fragments coexist with N/O-halogen bonds, N-S attachments, peroxide groups, acyl halides, cumulated unsaturation and fused small-ring or bridged systems. Aliphatic amines are already represented and sometimes strongly associated with high labels; it would be false to diagnose universal absence of basic nitrogen or rings. Neutral SMILES do not imply absence of physiological protonation. Structurally diverse accepted output narrows to recurrent within-seed high-label families; typed Murcko cores measure graph diversity, not independent chemically credible series. Child_complete and paired_complete are both true with all three matched seeds and no profile mismatch. Published Parent trajectories are the current comparison baseline. No supplied path, objective or pairing is missing. RDKit descriptors and observation-level motif counts, accepted row provenance, digest verification and input SHA256 hashes are in .slots/round-0027-slot-0/molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json and accepted_molecule_descriptors.jsonl. Original legal Search-history molecular reports were read through context.evidence_index for n-c55c3d520a2c, n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180; full_history_processed=false remains unresolved. Parent composition_status=needs_review remains an attribution obstacle requiring catalog_review; this assessment neither resolves composition nor attributes chemistry to an exponential mean, original residual covariance, sulfur gate, foundation or constituent. Whole-foundation m-4fa9546e559e, constituent contribution, joint interactions, chemical mediation and partial L07 composition gaps remain distinct. The older full-law experiment on an ungated Parent is conditional source evidence and does not supply a matched factorial comparison. Observed chemical changes have no labels for rejected/passive alternatives and establish no causal mediator or transfer efficacy. Historical generator gaps below retain their source nodes and Search/budget conditions.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer molecules have median 25 heavy atoms, three perceived rings and two aromatic rings; 622 of 870 have a conventional carbonyl amide substructure. Seed 0 ends with an indole hydrazide bearing a direct N-F bond. Seed 1's 25-heavy-atom leader is an N-acyl five-membered unsaturated heterocycle attached to a phenyl imine/carbonyl region and a fluorinated methylpyridyl ring. Seed 2's 26-heavy-atom leader combines an anilide, an allene substituent and an aromatic-labelled nine-membered diaza ring with N-OH substitution. Aromatic and carbonyl organization is recognizable, but the reactive and unusual ring details keep synthetic plausibility questionable. Sulfur-containing accepted observations are 424 versus Parent 251; conventional sulfur classes are not equivalent to routine stable chemistry.
liabilities: Direct N-F/N-Br substitution and N-S attachments persist. N-hydroxy chemistry must be assessed separately from N-halogen bonds.

Non-sulfur cumulated-double-bond motifs occur in 106 accepted optimizer observations versus Parent 1, including the seed-2 allene; allene presence alone is not a universal instability test, but this complex ring arrangement warrants scrutiny.
The seed-1 leader has an unassigned potential stereogenic centre; none of the accepted optimizer SMILES specifies a stereocentre.
missing_features: Independent conventional realizations of the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are not consistently demonstrated among leaders; equal Br/F scores give no evidence that a particular halogen is essential.

Geometrically conventional alternatives to the aromatic-labelled nine-membered ring/allene combination, and specified stereochemistry for the saturated seed-1 ring centre, are not established. Their absence does not prove that the objective scores those missing properties.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Gap source n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced by n-62daf219c70a and carried by sulfur-gated n-1744a1494180; re-observed here in n-14a52e3f8725 under the frozen current profile, issued Search seeds 0/1/2 and 300 accepted observations per objective. The accepted output still includes direct N/O-halogen bonds, peroxide, N-S and acyl-halide motifs, including high-label reactive exceptions. One direct N-halogen incidence decreases from Parent 425 to Child 51 observations while O-halogen rises from 82 to 130 and acyl-halide from 0 to 26 in the same anonymous objective stream. Those counts describe observed molecules and do not establish mechanism attribution, safety, synthesis or a causal chemical mediator.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while keeping useful aromatic and polar-group organization.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs sensitivity to intact local functional-group environments and conventional alternatives that preserve learned molecular relationships. Treat the inherited sulfur signature envelope as a narrow admission condition, not as comprehensive chemistry validation. Any intervention would need its own authorized, objective-blind test; score associations here do not authorize blanket removal or task-specific copying.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180; current n-14a52e3f8725 accepted Search output under the supplied three-seed/budget/profile scope retains a cyclic cumulene, three- and four-membered fused systems, multiply closed unsaturated rings and an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring. These occur among high-label molecules, not only weak fragments. All accepted molecules parse, demonstrating the distinction between graph validity and geometric feasibility. No rejected/passive alternative has a reward, and no component-specific mediation is established.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can represent ring graphs without consistently supplying geometrically credible unsaturation, fusion and bridge topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need awareness of ring size, permitted unsaturation geometry and bridge/fusion connectivity, together with feasible alternatives retaining useful functional-group relations. Preserve valid ordinary small-ring motifs where appropriate; a small-ring count alone cannot distinguish acceptable saturated rings from difficult fused unsaturation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and persists through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180 to n-14a52e3f8725 under issued Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 accepted observations per objective and the frozen current profile. All Child optimizer digest stereocentre-string rates are 0.0, while parsed leading aromatic/aliphatic amines carry unassigned potential centres. The three leaders in one anonymous objective stream contain five, two and one such centres. Neutral SMILES similarly leave protonation unresolved but do not imply absence of basic amines. Labels do not compare stereoisomers or measured protonation states.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged arrangements remain incompletely specified by the generator.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or specify meaningful stereochemistry as graph edits create stable potential stereocentres, while treating achiral and configurationally unstable cases appropriately. Protonation and tautomer identity require separate handling. This is a representation gap, not proof that stereochemical resolution changes any score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a; re-observed in n-14a52e3f8725 against sulfur-gated n-1744a1494180 on the same frozen three-seed accepted Search panel. Tiny fragment examples approach observed score floors, while complete aromatic/polar arrangements are stronger. Another stream expands from Parent median 31 to Child median 45 heavy atoms with a Child maximum 119, but its upper-label quartile median 38 is below lower-quartile 46.5. The stream is not named as a prescription; the association neither proves a universal size cap nor attributes fragmentation or growth to one component.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator inconsistently retains enough structural context while avoiding weak fragmentation and excessive linked-ring elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator should preserve useful connected functional relationships through fragmentation/recombination and offer alternate compact architectures rather than repeatedly severing context or appending rings. Any contextual control must learn only from its legal task-local accepted feedback and retain evidence for adverse or unchanged cases.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a, this remains conditional evidence in n-14a52e3f8725 versus current Parent n-1744a1494180 under the frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 and accepted budget. Upper-label quarters concentrate into 29, 39 or 60 typed graph cores in some streams, while lower-label quarters contain 125, 111 or 173, respectively. Multiple labelled examples differ only in a halogen, side chain or local ring connection; exact label ties coexist with large plausibility differences. Core novelty is not independently validated chemistry or useful exploration, and no independent seed replication, component interaction or chemical mediator is established.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph variation does not consistently yield chemically independent credible alternatives to each seed’s leading molecular family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic proposal process needs access to alternative feasible core arrangements preserving useful relationships, with real accepted feedback establishing whether they improve absolute quality. Do not equate new graph cores, lower reactive-bond counts or relative parent wins with productive new chemistry; preserve source conditions and negative comparisons when transferring this gap.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
